text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Generale des Eaux becomes majority shareholder of media group Havas with a 30 percent stake, Havas to become the majority shareholder in pay-TV channel Canal Plus with a 34.4 percent stake, once the latter's merger with Nethold is effective. Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier in an interview says that he does not rule out disengaging from advertising and tourism activities.
-- CDR structure selling off Credit Lyonnais assets sold 4.6 percent of Rhone Poulenc 's capital.
-- Experts' report criticises state for its management of insurer GAN and its banking subsidiary CIC, on grounds that property-related risks were under-estimated in subsidiary UIC-Sofal.
-- GDF utility posts a record 2.6 billion francs profit for 1996.

-- Junior budget minister Alain Lamassoure in an interview says European construction is the best way to resist global competition and tackle global markets, adds mandatory contributions should be consistent throughout Europe, implying a possible cut in French taxes.
-- Finance Ministry seeks to freeze some 15 billion francs to prevent possible excess spending ahead of 1998 legislative election.
-- State to buy Credit Lyonnais's stake in Thomson SA for an estimated 2.9 billion francs before before Feb 23, as part of an April 1996 agreement designed to ease a planned Thomson privatisation.
-- Germany shaken by unemployment rate of 12.2 percent.
